chunks: I heard ʿAlī ibn Jaʿfar narrating to al-Ḥasan ibn al-Ḥusayn ibn ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥusayn, and he said: “By Allah, Allah certainly granted victory to Abū al-Ḥasan al-Riḍā عليه السلام.” So al-Ḥasan said to him: “Yes, by Allah, may I be sacrificed for you, his brothers surely transgressed against him.” So ʿAlī ibn Jaʿfar said: “Yes, by Allah, and we, his paternal uncles, transgressed against him.”

So al-Ḥasan said to him: “May I be sacrificed for you, what did you do? For I was not present with you.” He said: “His brothers said to him, and we as well: ‘There has never been among us an Imam of altered complexion.’ So al-Riḍā عليه السلام said to them: ‘He is my son.’ They said: ‘The Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله judged by al-qāfah, so between us and you is al-qāfah.’ He said: ‘You send to them yourselves. As for me, no. And do not inform them why you invited them, and let yourselves remain in your houses.’”

So when they came, they seated us in the orchard, and his paternal uncles, his brothers, and his sisters lined up. They took al-Riḍā عليه السلام, clothed him in a woolen robe and a cap of it, placed a spade on his neck, and said to him: ‘Enter the orchard as though you are working in it.’ Then they brought Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام and said: ‘Attach this boy to his father.’ They said: ‘He has no father here, but this is his father’s uncle, and this is his father’s uncle, and this is his uncle, and this is his paternal aunt. But if he has a father here, then he is the owner of the orchard, for his feet and his feet are one.’ So when Abū al-Ḥasan عليه السلام returned, they said: ‘This is his father.’

ʿAlī ibn Jaʿfar said: “So I stood up and sucked the saliva of Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام, then I said to him: ‘I bear witness that you are my Imam before Allah.’ Then al-Riḍā عليه السلام wept and said: ‘O uncle, did you not hear my father while he was saying: The Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله said: “May my father be for the son of the best of the slave-women, the son of the Nubian woman, pure of mouth, select of womb. Woe to them! May Allah curse al-Uʿaybis and his offspring, the possessor of tribulation. He will kill them for years and months and days, impose abasement upon them, and give them to drink a goblet that causes endurance. And he is the outcast, the fugitive, the one bereaved through his father and his grandfather, the possessor of the ghaybah, about whom it will be said: He died or he perished; in which valley did he travel?” O uncle, can this be anyone but me?’ So I said: ‘You have spoken the truth, may I be sacrificed for you.’”

key_terms.أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ: Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام, identified here as the son of al-Riḍā عليه السلام
key_terms.إِمَامٌ: Imam; the divinely designated religious authority being discussed in the narration
key_terms.الشَّرِيدُ: the fugitive or displaced one; part of the description of the Imam in trial
key_terms.الطَّرِيدُ: the outcast; a description in the reported prophetic wording
key_terms.الْبُسْتَانِ: the orchard where the test of resemblance was arranged
key_terms.الْغَيْبَةِ: the ghaybah; the occultation mentioned in the hadith
key_terms.الْفِتْنَةِ: tribulation or strife associated with the persecuting force mentioned in the report
key_terms.الْقَافَةُ: physiognomic identification used here to determine family resemblance

ai.seo_question: How does this hadith describe the recognition of Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام and the prophetic indication of the ghaybah?
ai.summary: This narration recounts how the paternity of Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام was publicly confirmed in response to objections raised by some of Imam al-Riḍā’s عليه السلام relatives. It then moves from that episode to a declaration of his Imamate and a prophetic tradition indicating the lineage, trials, and ghaybah of a later Imam, highlighting continuity of divine designation within the Ahl al-Bayt عليهم السلام.
